meta.title: An Email About a Family Dinner

paragraphs: Subject: A Family Dinner. Dear Grace, Thank you for your email and for your drawing of the cat. I love the colors! How is your violin? I hope that you and your family are well. School is busy, because we have a math test on Tuesday. Now I want to tell you about my Sunday.

Uncle Dan is my dad's older brother. Uncle Dan and his wife came to our house at noon. They live in another town, so we do not see them often. They brought bags of fresh fruit from the market. Mom said, "Today we will cook together." First, we watched a short video about banana fritters. Dad downloaded it on Saturday night. I think that technology is very useful in the kitchen. But we still need our hands!

The recipe has five ingredients: bananas, flour, sugar, coconut milk, and water. The bananas were cheap, and they cost twenty baht per kilo. Tom cut the bananas into small pieces. I mixed the flour, the sugar, the coconut milk, and the water in a big bowl. Then I put the banana pieces in the bowl. Uncle Dan's wife poured oil into a deep pan. Mom said, "Hot oil is dangerous." The oil was very hot, so Mom did the cooking. The kitchen smelled sweet and warm. Pip walked around the kitchen and looked at the bananas.

We ate at five o'clock in the garden. The fritters were hot, sweet, and very good. Pip sat under the table and waited for a piece. Uncle Dan said, "These are the best fritters in the family!" Tom ate seven fritters, and I ate only four. Everybody laughed, and Pip barked. After dinner, I washed the bowl and the spoons. Uncle Dan and his wife went home before dark.

What do you cook with your family? Please tell me about your favorite dish. If you send me a recipe, I will cook it with Mom. Please say hello to Ms. Ong and to your class. I will send you a photo of our fritters. Please write soon. Best wishes, Lily.
text.summary: Lily writes an email to her pen pal Grace about a family Sunday. Uncle Dan and his wife visit, and the family cooks banana fritters from a video recipe.
